rationale: C21 is a direct and material drafting precursor. It delegates and organizes functions under the Defense Production Act of 1950, expressly reserves presidential control over regulations under sections 710(b), 710(c), and 710(d), and authorizes officers or agencies receiving functions under C21 to exercise related Title VII powers. The child expressly identifies the heads of departments or agencies receiving functions under the September 9, 1950 directive and then supplies the reserved section 710(b)-(d) personnel delegations, restrictions, conflict rules, certifications, filings, and review procedures. Thus the child is effectively a personnel-focused continuation of C21's administrative machinery. C06 has some overlap concerning voluntary and uncompensated personnel and classification rules, while C18 concerns defense-related personnel procedures, but neither shows the direct statutory and cross-directive linkage of C21.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The head of any department or agency delegated or assigned functions under the Act pursuant to [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], of September 9, 1950, is hereby delegated the authority provided by subsection 710(b) of that Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each officer or agency having functions under the Defense Production Act of 1950 delegated or assigned thereto by this Executive order may exercise and perform, with respect to such functions, the functions vested in the President by Title VII of the said Act.
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly uses the class of officials created by C21's delegation scheme as the recipients of additional Defense Production Act authority.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Such heads of departments or agencies are further delegated the authority provided by subsection 710(c) of that Act ... [and] subsection 710(d)
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There are excluded from the functions delegated by section 902(a) of this Executive order ... the functions of the President with respect to regulations under sections 710(b), 710(c), and 710(d) of the said Act
shared_material.explanation: C21 specifically withholds the exact three personnel authorities that the child subsequently delegates and regulates, demonstrating complementary legal machinery rather than mere topical similarity.

shared_material.child_excerpt: At least once every three months, the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission shall survey appointments made under this order and shall report his findings to the President and make such recommendations as he may deem proper.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each officer or agency ... shall submit to the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission such requests for classification of positions ... and shall accompany any such request with a certificate stating that the duties of the position are essential and appropriate for the administration of the said Act.
shared_material.explanation: Both directives place Defense Production Act staffing under Civil Service Commission oversight using certifications, review, and reporting, with the child extending that supervisory framework to the specially appointed personnel.
